display.title: Episode 23: The Needles and Toothpicks, Chapter 2 (Lag BaOmer)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's Lag BaOmer show: why children carry bows and arrows, the funny ending of the needles and toothpicks story, a listener's poem, and a Sefer Torah for every child.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Lag BaOmer 5742, the first show with music after the Sefirah weeks. Uncle Yossi explains why Lag BaOmer is Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's day of joy, and why children take bows and arrows on their outings: in his time, children learned Torah hidden in the forest and pretended to play archery whenever officers came by. After the Hakochainik march, a yeshiva boy recites the Shema in Studio 604. Then the story of the king's question is resolved. Reuven sends Shimon's worthless toothpicks and needles to the fair with two expert salesmen, who meet, swap the goods and both bring home the very same junk. Reuven explains that Shimon traded gold for junk, while they only traded junk for junk; the rabbi tells the king that this is why turning from Hashem to idols is so much worse for the Jewish people. A listener's letter and poem are read, and Uncle Yossi compares the Torah to the cement that holds bricks together, inviting every child to buy a letter in a new Sefer Torah.
display.lesson: Like the children of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's time, treasure the Torah; turning away from Hashem is like trading gold for worthless junk.
